walkthroughs.body_html:
Numerical Methods — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numerical Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numerical Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Using Newton-Raphson on f(x) = x² − 2 with x₀ = 1.5, what is x₁? (Give to 3 dp.)
The trapezium rule estimates which kind of quantity?
options: a definite integral
a derivative
a sum to infinity
a stationary point
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
1/6 — by multiplying the denominators only.

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.
It means the vectors are parallel.
1/6 — by multiplying the denominators only.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
2/5 — by adding numerators and denominators separately.
5/6 — find common denominators (3/6 + 2/6).
1/6 — by multiplying the denominators only.
